messages:
Alex W: quick thought — can we consider a hybrid API key model for service auth? mix of long-lived project keys + short-lived tenant-scoped ephemeral tokens. want to reduce token surface but keep operator ergonomics. :thinking:
Priya: curious, how do you see rollout? do you mean issue ephemeral tokens from a broker that mints on-demand?
Alex W: yea, broker service that mints short-lived bearer tokens scoped to org/project claims. keep legacy keys as a fallback but mark them as 'admin-only' and audit.
Morgan: main tradeoff is runtime checks & cache invalidation. ephemeral tokens mean we can avoid revocation lists but need fast introspection or JWT validation with rotating keys.
Dan: also watch routing — some infra paths only accept project-scoped keys today. adding ephemeral org tokens could break per-route authorizers unless we add a claim normalization layer.
Priya: normalization layer ok, but we should avoid adding a synchronous call on each request. prefer verifying JWT signature + local claim-to-role mapping. update the role map on rotation events.
Alex W: agreed. proposal: broker returns JWTs signed by a short-lived KID; edge verifies signature locally using cached jwks and maps claims -> RBAC roles. no network hop for success paths. on jwks rotation, edges fetch new keys async.
Morgan: sounds good. how about token binding for service-to-service? we still rely on mTLS in some clusters. tokens alone feel weaker for internal traffic.
Alex W: keep mTLS for intra-cluster mutual auth; tokens are primarily for external service integrations and user-facing service accounts.
Dan: for fallback legacy keys, we should implement an 'elevated-priv' flag and force route-level require_admin checks. plus telemetry to show usage so we can sunset.
Priya: can we have a short retention policy: legacy keys expire in 6mo unless reapproved? automation can email owners.
Alex W: yep — lifecycle plan: (1) broker + jwks-based validation, (2) role-mapping layer in the authorizer, (3) legacy key flag + telemetry + 6mo expiry, (4) rollout in canary clusters.
Morgan: one more nit: what if a request comes with an ephemeral token but the org claim references a project that doesn't exist (race during provisioning)? should default to deny and emit audit with reason "unknown_project".
Dan: deny + audit is safest. maybe add a short grace cache for new projects (30s) to reduce flakiness during rollout.
Priya: security question — how do we prevent broker abuse? rate-limit mint operations per service principal and require proof-of-possession for high-priv tokens.
Alex W: yep add mint quotas + PoP for role>admin tokens (e.g., signed key handle). also require rotation of broker creds and KMS-backed signing.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: auth-broker v0.2 -> canary on prod-cluster-3 at 2026-03-25T02:00Z.
Alex W: OK let's draft a short RFC with these sections: threat model, broker design, jwks rotation, role normalization, legacy key migration plan, rollout checklist. I'll start a draft and tag you all. :thumbsup:
Priya: thanks — i'll add the RBAC mapping appendix and some rollout test cases.
Morgan: i'll write the jwks rotation doc and local validator checklist.
Dan: i'll add the telemetry + admin-fallback policy.
Alex W: sweet — tagging followups in the RFC. if anyone has objections speak now, otherwise i'll open PR.
